column1: # Real Li-ion electrolyte anions. Charge is EXPLICIT and the spelling convention is pinned
# per row -- see docs/track2_chemistry_spec.md §6. Dual use: Track 2 L3, and Track 1's anion
# fine-tune, which trains on the 19 non-EXCLUDED rows (widened at 4c0b0c2; the header previously
# said five and was stale). G1 there is a memorization check by construction either way: fine-tuning
# on 19 and scoring reconstruction on the same 19 is in-sample.
# EXCLUSIONS ARE CHEMISTRY, NOT TOKENIZATION. Both excluded rows are out of Track 2's ELEMENT SET,
# and the element set is a decision about what the molecular universe contains -- independent of
# any tokenizer. That AsF6 also happens to add a character under the char tokenizer is incidental
# and is NOT the reason; a tokenizer change does not reopen either row.
# `alphabet_ok` is measured, not asserted: whether the SMILES stays inside ZINC-250k's

column5: MEASURED: both the hypervalent and the charge-separated spelling canonicalize to [O-][Cl+3]([O-])([O-])[O-], which is the catalog's stored form. Not ambiguous AFTER canonicalization
MEASURED: canonicalizes to the catalog's stored TFSI exactly. Charge on N
MEASURED: canonicalizes to the catalog's stored FSI exactly. Charge on N
ALIAS: also written ODFB (lithium oxalyldifluoroborate). Same anion, BF2(C2O4)-; both abbreviations are in common use. Recorded so a search for ODFB does not conclude it is absent.
aromatic anion; charge on ring N
charge-separated is the standard spelling here
single atom; real in some Li-S / conversion chemistries

EXCLUDED from the element set (As). CHEMISTRY REASON: LiAsF6 is a real historical Li-ion salt, abandoned on arsenic toxicity rather than on performance. Listed so its absence is deliberate rather than an oversight

EXCLUDED from the element set (Br). CHEMISTRY REASON: bromide is oxidised well below the cathode potentials these formulations target, so it is not a stable anion in a 4 V cell. Listed for the same reason
